title: macOS: one ~25–40 ms main-thread stall ~15 s after every launch — AppKit state-restoration initial flush, although Godot's windows are not restorable
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4], both the standard and the .NET build.
- Both rendering drivers: Metal and Vulkan (MoltenVK), Forward+.

### System information

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M5 Pro (18 cores, 64 GB), built-in display at 120 Hz. Windowed, V-Sync enabled.

### Issue description

The project below does nothing except log frame intervals from one Node2D. It still drops one long frame, 24–40 ms at 120 Hz, **~15.07 s after engine start, in every launch**:
- The instant is the same within ±40 ms on the standard and .NET builds, on both drivers.
- In a game it lands mid-play as a visible hitch.

**Where the frame goes.** I timestamped the first and last `_process`, `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` / `frame_post_draw`, and an `InputEventAction` injected each frame and seen in `_input` at the next event flush.
- The whole stall falls **after `frame_post_draw` and before the next input flush**. That is between iterations, in the AppKit run loop, not in scripts, physics or rendering.
- On that frame the viewport's CPU render time is ~0.1 ms.

**What runs there.** The unified log shows, at the same instant, on the **main thread**:

```
21:26:23.263 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges]
21:26:23.263 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges] Emptying for initial flush.
21:26:23.291 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges] finishing enqueued operations
```

- The "initial flush" took 16–28 ms on the main thread in 14 of 14 launches I matched against the log.
- Later flushes are coalesced to ~15 s and much cheaper (1–9 ms).

**Godot doesn't use this feature.**
- Every window is already opted out of restoration: `[wd.window_object setRestorable:NO]` in `platform/macos/display_server_macos.mm`.
- `GodotApplicationDelegate` answers `applicationSupportsSecureRestorableState:` with YES.
- The app-level `NSPersistentUIManager` still runs, and its first flush is the cost.

**Cause confirmed.** Turning the per-app Resume switch off through the argument domain, `-ApplePersistence NO` (AppKit echoes `ApplePersistence=NO` on stderr), removes both the StateRestoration log lines and the stall:
- With the flag: 0 of 5 launches stalled at ~15 s (Metal and Vulkan, standard and .NET).
- Without it: 19 of 20 launches stalled.
- `-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES` does **not** help: 5 of 5 launches still flushed and stalled.

With the MRP below on the official standard build, Metal, 120 Hz:

```
control #1:  long frame 35.1 ms, ending at 15.074 s   | log: initial flush 22:25:12.661 -> .687 (26 ms)
control #2:  long frame 36.3 ms, ending at 15.076 s   | log: initial flush 22:25:58.566 -> .594 (28 ms)
-ApplePersistence NO #1, #2:  no long frame near 15 s, no StateRestoration lines
```

A later independent re-run on the same machine gave control 33.9 ms at 15.066 s and 35.9 ms at 15.069 s. With the flag, nothing near 15 s.

Other long frames in the output (18–80 ms, irregular) are not this bug. They are waits inside `RenderingServer.draw` for the compositor, and they line up with system activity: the menu-bar clock's minute tick and Wi-Fi daemon log bursts.

**Possible fix.** Opt the process out of AppKit persistence before `NSApplication` finishes launching, for example early in `main()` in `platform/macos/godot_main_macos.mm`:

```objc
[[NSUserDefaults standardUserDefaults] registerDefaults:@{ @"ApplePersistence" : @NO }];
```

- The registration domain is the lowest-priority defaults domain, so a user or an exported app can still turn it back on.
- Every Godot window is already non-restorable, so nothing user-visible should change.
- If something relies on app-level restoration, this could go behind a project setting.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create the three files below in an empty folder, `persistent_ui_flush_repro/`.
2. Run it from a terminal so stdout is visible:
   `Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --path persistent_ui_flush_repro res://main.tscn`
   It quits by itself after 22 s.
3. Observe `long frame XX ms, ending at ~15.07 s after engine start`.
4. Optional: in another terminal, run
   `log stream --style compact --predicate 'process == "Godot" AND category == "StateRestoration"'`.
   The `Emptying for initial flush` line lands on the same instant.
5. Run again with `-ApplePersistence NO` appended after the scene path. Before it, a bare `NO` would be taken as the positional scene argument.
   The ~15 s long frame and the log lines are gone.

Expected: no main-thread stall from a restoration feature Godot does not use.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Three files, inlined:

`project.godot`
```ini
config_version=5

[application]

config/name="persistent_ui_flush_repro"
run/main_scene="res://main.tscn"
config/features=PackedStringArray("4.6", "Forward Plus")
```

`main.tscn`
```
[gd_scene load_steps=2 format=3]

[ext_resource type="Script" path="res://main.gd" id="1"]

[node name="Main" type="Node2D"]
script = ExtResource("1")
```

`main.gd`
```gdscript
extends Node2D
## Prints every frame whose _process-to-_process interval exceeds LONG_MS, stamped with the engine
## clock (seconds since engine start), then quits after RUN_S. Nothing else runs in this project.

const LONG_MS := 18.0
const RUN_S := 22.0

var _last_usec := 0


func _ready() -> void:
	print("driver=%s vsync=%d refresh=%.0f Hz" % [RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_driver_name(),
		DisplayServer.window_get_vsync_mode(), DisplayServer.screen_get_refresh_rate()])


func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	var now := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	if _last_usec > 0 and now - _last_usec > LONG_MS * 1000.0:
		print("long frame %.1f ms, ending at %.3f s after engine start" % [(now - _last_usec) / 1000.0, now / 1e6])
	_last_usec = now
	if now > RUN_S * 1e6:
		get_tree().quit()
```
